title: Google’s Pixel Watch 5 dives deeper into AI and health
excerpt: The $399 Google Pixel Watch 5 doesn’t change much in terms of hardware, but it features a ton of new AI and health updates.
content_html:
The $399 Google Pixel Watch 5 isn’t about the hardware. Sure, there’s a new satin pyrite case finish, a few new strap colors, and a Steph Curry Special Edition. Under the hood, there’s a slightly faster Qualcomm processor and an itty-bitty battery bump. There’s a $50 price hike from last year, too, because the Pixel Watch 5 isn’t immune to RAMageddon — none of us are. Otherwise, no one would blame you for looking at this watch and thinking absolutely nothing’s changed. That’s because the big updates this year are all software-based.

This isn’t a huge surprise considering Google’s Fitbit Air launch in May. And after seeing some Pixel Watch 5 demos, it’s clear this year’s refresh is furthering the AI and proactive health themes that Google introduced earlier this year.

Health and fitness features account for the bulk of the updates, but Gemini on the wrist gets a few key improvements. You can now use it offline for simple tasks like starting timers and launching apps. (Though I noticed in my demo it was notably slower when doing this offline.) Gemini will also be more proactive in making suggestions. One example I saw: a text asking for my availability brought up the option to check Google Calendar from the wrist. Likewise, there’s now an icon right on the watchface that surfaces real-time information for things like timers, Uber ETAs, and workouts. Meanwhile, the pinchy pinch and wrist-flick features came via a software update to Pixel Watches in December, but they’re much more fully integrated into the UI with WearOS 7.

You can also use AI to generate watchfaces. I created a watchface featuring “fat cats and an elegant font.” It didn’t quite do that. The fat cats weren’t characters, so much as pleasantly plump, cat-shaped clock numbers. It’s a gimmicky way to shoehorn the Nano Banana model onto the watch… but if that’s your thing, it works.

Now for the health stuff. The most novel update is Breathing Emergency Detection. It’s an extension of last year’s Loss of Pulse feature. When the watch detects a severe drop in blood oxygen saturation (aka SpO2), it’ll trigger a call to emergency services and your designated emergency contacts. (A sudden drop in SpO2 may indicate you’re struggling to breathe.) To minimize false positives, the watch uses a combination of heart rate, motion, and altitude sensors. While I didn’t get to see the feature in action, I was told at my demo that the feature won’t kick in unless SpO2 drops to roughly 83 percent — so a significant decrease — for an extended period. It also disables once the watch determines you’ve been asleep for 30 minutes to mitigate false alarms linked to low SpO2 from sleep apnea or side sleeping. The feature also isn’t intended to be used by people with preexisting or chronic respiratory conditions; it’s more for flagging acute instances where a person may have stopped breathing. It’ll be available on both the Pixel Watch 4 and 5 in Europe at launch, and is pending clearance from the FDA in the US.

A less high-stakes feature is that the Pixel Watch (and Fitbit Air) will also track nightly sleep breathing quality and provide monthly updates. The idea is to see how your daily trends impact respiratory health at night over a longer time frame.

Two other health features are blood pressure trends and insulin resistance trends. First and foremost: Neither of these is diagnostic. Both are wellness features intended to function as “check engine light”-type warnings, require a minimum of a week’s worth of data, and flag trends monthly. They won’t be available right when the Pixel Watch 5 launches; rollout is currently scheduled for September. That said, these features will also come to the Pixel Watch 3 or later, as well as the Fitbit Air.

With blood pressure trends, the watch will monitor blood flow using the optical heart rate sensor, as well as motion sensors. That data gets fed into an AI model to estimate the shape and speed of pulse waves traveling under the skin to approximate whether your blood pressure is trending higher or lower. (There will be no direct systolic or diastolic measurements.)

While we’ve seen other wearable players like Apple and Whoop tackle blood pressure insights, Google’s attempt at non-invasive insulin resistance detection is brand spanking new. Insulin resistance describes a condition in which your body doesn’t metabolize food effectively. The pancreas has to produce more insulin to utilize blood glucose, and untreated, it often leads to fatigue, stubborn weight gain, and eventually, Type 2 diabetes. This feature would passively estimate whether your insulin resistance is trending higher or lower month to month based on signals like heart rhythm, sleep quality, and daily movements. To validate the algorithm, Google says it tested the algorithm against blood draws and published its findings in a peer-reviewed study in Nature.

1/5

Photo: Victoria Song / The Verge

Again, this is not noninvasive blood glucose monitoring. As with blood pressure trends, there are no direct readings involved, and this isn’t a screening feature for diabetes. It’s just flagging when your lifestyle trends indicate sustained metabolic stress over a monthlong period. Even so, I’ve spilled a ton of ink on the decadelong process for me to get diagnosed with insulin resistance. It can remain asymptomatic for several years, it may not show up in routine metabolic tests, and a traditional diagnosis involves nagging doctors to test fasting insulin and glucose via blood draws. We’ll have to see how this feature works in real life, but it’s potentially huge if it works well.

That’s health. Google isn’t slacking on the fitness front either. Fitbit and Pixel Watch users have griped for years over dubious GPS maps from outdoor activities, especially in urban areas. Last year, Google introduced dual-frequency GPS. This year, it’s making the bold claim that the Pixel Watch 5 will outperform the Garmin Fenix 8 and Apple Watch Ultra 3 by utilizing satellite and weather station data, as well as 3D models of buildings from Google Maps, to “correct” GPS data using AI in post-processing. Shots fired.

Google is also bringing AI-generated strength training plans to the wrist. This feature is already available with Google Health Premium, but the difference is that you no longer need the phone to log reps or move on to the next exercise. At least based on my demo, this seems like an obvious and smart move given the renewed emphasis on strength training in the GLP-1 era.

All of these health updates are meant to feed into the Google Health app’s AI coach (which requires a Google Health Premium subscription). As I wrote in my Fitbit Air review, Google’s AI coach is the best of the lot — but that is a remarkably low bar at the moment. AI health remains a work in progress, and Google’s coach is no exception — but so far these updates are a savvy mix of potentially helpful and smart for building a long-term AI health roadmap.

The Google Pixel Watch 5 is available for preorder starting today and arrives on shelves August 20th. The Steph Curry Special Edition will hit shelves September 3rd.

blocks.html_en: Again, this is not noninvasive blood glucose monitoring. As with blood pressure trends, there are no direct readings involved, and this isn’t a screening feature for diabetes. It’s just flagging when your lifestyle trends indicate sustained metabolic stress over a monthlong period. Even so, I’ve spilled a ton of ink on the decadelong process for me to get diagnosed with insulin resistance. It can remain asymptomatic for several years, it may not show up in routine metabolic tests, and a traditional diagnosis involves nagging doctors to test fasting insulin and glucose via blood draws. We’ll have to see how this feature works in real life, but it’s potentially huge if it works well.

blocks.html_en: That’s health. Google isn’t slacking on the fitness front either. Fitbit and Pixel Watch users have griped for years over dubious GPS maps from outdoor activities, especially in urban areas. Last year, Google introduced dual-frequency GPS. This year, it’s making the bold claim that the Pixel Watch 5 will outperform the Garmin Fenix 8 and Apple Watch Ultra 3 by utilizing satellite and weather station data, as well as 3D models of buildings from Google Maps, to “correct” GPS data using AI in post-processing. Shots fired.

sentences.en: Victoria Song

content_html_zh:
售价 399 美元的 Google Pixel Watch 5 与硬件无关。 当然，还有新的缎面黄铁矿表壳、一些新的表带颜色以及斯蒂芬·库里特别版。 在引擎盖下，有一个稍快的高通处理器和一个很小的电池凸起。 价格也比去年上涨了 50 美元，因为 Pixel Watch 5 也不能幸免于 RAMgeddon——我们都不能幸免。 否则，没有人会责怪您看着这款手表并认为绝对没有任何变化。 这是因为今年的重大更新都是基于软件的。

考虑到谷歌五月份推出的 Fitbit Air，这并不令人意外。 在看过一些 Pixel Watch 5 演示后，很明显，今年的更新正在进一步推进谷歌今年早些时候推出的人工智能和主动健康主题。

健康和健身功能占了更新的大部分，但手腕上的 Gemini 得到了一些关键改进。 您现在可以离线使用它来执行简单的任务，例如启动计时器和启动应用程序。 （尽管我在演示中注意到，离线执行此操作时速度明显较慢。） 双子座也会更加主动地提出建议。 我看到的一个例子：一条询问我是否有空的短信显示了从手腕上查看 Google 日历的选项。 同样，现在表盘上有一个图标，可以显示计时器、Uber ETA 和锻炼等实时信息。 与此同时，捏捏和手腕轻弹功能是通过 12 月份 Pixel 手表的软件更新实现的，但它们通过 WearOS 7 更完全地集成到 UI 中。

您还可以使用人工智能生成表盘。 我创建了一个以“肥猫和优雅字体”为特色的表盘。 但它并没有完全做到这一点。 这些肥猫不是角色，而是令人愉悦的丰满的猫形时钟数字。 这是将 Nano Banana 模型硬塞到手表上的一种噱头…… 但如果那是你的事，那就行了。

现在来说说健康方面的事情。 最新颖的更新是呼吸紧急检测。 这是去年“失去脉搏”功能的延伸。 当手表检测到血氧饱和度（又名 SpO2）严重下降时，它会触发紧急服务和您指定的紧急联系人的呼叫。 （SpO2 突然下降可能表明您呼吸困难。） 为了最大限度地减少误报，该手表结合使用了心率、运动和海拔传感器。 虽然我没有看到该功能的实际应用，但在演示中我被告知，除非 SpO2 在较长时间内下降到大约 83%（如此显着的下降），否则该功能不会启动。 一旦手表确定您已经睡了 30 分钟，它也会禁用，以减少与睡眠呼吸暂停或侧睡导致的低 SpO2 相关的误报。 该功能也不适合患有现有或慢性呼吸道疾病的人使用。它更适合标记一个人可能停止呼吸的紧急情况。 该功能在欧洲推出时将在 Pixel Watch 4 和 5 上使用，目前正在等待美国 FDA 的批准。

一个不太高风险的功能是 Pixel Watch（和 Fitbit Air）还将跟踪夜间睡眠呼吸质量并提供每月更新。 这个想法是为了了解您的日常趋势如何在较长时间内影响夜间的呼吸健康。

另外两个健康特征是血压趋势和胰岛素抵抗趋势。 首先也是最重要的：这些都不是诊断性的。 两者都是健康功能，旨在充当“检查引擎灯”类型的警告，需要至少一周的数据，并每月标记趋势。 Pixel Watch 5 发布时它们还不会立即上市；目前计划于 9 月推出。 也就是说，这些功能也将出现在 Pixel Watch 3 或更高版本以及 Fitbit Air 上。

根据血压趋势，手表将使用光学心率传感器和运动传感器监测血流。 这些数据被输入人工智能模型，以估计皮下传播的脉搏波的形状和速度，从而估算出您的血压是升高还是降低。 （不会有直接的收缩压或舒张压测量。）

虽然我们已经看到苹果和 Whoop 等其他可穿戴设备厂商在解决血压洞察问题，但谷歌在非侵入性胰岛素抵抗检测方面的尝试是全新的。 胰岛素抵抗是指您的身体无法有效代谢食物的情况。 胰腺必须产生更多的胰岛素来利用血糖，如果不加以治疗，通常会导致疲劳、体重持续增加，并最终导致 2 型糖尿病。 此功能将根据心律、睡眠质量和日常运动等信号，被动地估计您的胰岛素抵抗是否逐月升高或降低。 为了验证该算法，谷歌表示，它针对抽血测试了该算法，并在《自然》杂志的一项同行评审研究中发表了其研究结果。

1/5Pixel Watch 3 及更高版本以及 Fitbit Air 将于 9 月推出。 照片：宋茜/The Verge

再次强调，这不是无创血糖监测。 与血压趋势一样，不涉及直接读数，这不是糖尿病的筛查功能。 当您的生活方式趋势表明一个月内持续存在代谢压力时，它就会减弱。 即便如此，我还是在长达十年的被诊断出胰岛素抵抗的过程中花费了大量的笔墨。 它可以在数年内保持无症状，可能不会出现在常规代谢测试中，传统的诊断包括让医生通过抽血测试空腹胰岛素和血糖。 我们必须看看这个功能在现实生活中是如何运作的，但如果运作良好，它的潜力将是巨大的。

这就是健康。 谷歌在健身方面也没有懈怠。 Fitbit 和 Pixel Watch 用户多年来一直对户外活动（尤其是在城市地区）的可疑 GPS 地图感到不满。 去年，谷歌推出了双频GPS。 今年，它大胆宣称 Pixel Watch 5 将利用卫星和气象站数据以及 Google 地图中的建筑物 3D 模型，在后处理中使用人工智能“纠正”GPS 数据，从而超越 Garmin Fenix 8 和 Apple Watch Ultra 3。 开枪了。

谷歌还将人工智能生成的力量训练计划带到了手腕上。 Google Health Premium 已提供此功能，但不同之处在于您不再需要手机来记录重复次数或继续进行下一个锻炼。 至少根据我的演示，考虑到 GLP-1 时代重新强调力量训练，这似乎是一个明显且明智的举措。

所有这些健康更新都旨在输入 Google Health 应用程序的 AI 教练（需要订阅 Google Health Premium）。 正如我在 Fitbit Air 评论中所写，谷歌的人工智能教练是最好的——但目前这个标准非常低。 人工智能健康仍然是一项正在进行的工作，谷歌的教练也不例外——但到目前为止，这些更新是构建长期人工智能健康路线图的潜在帮助和智能的精明组合。

Google Pixel Watch 5 即日起接受预订，并于 8 月 20 日上架。 斯蒂芬·库里特别版将于 9 月 3 日上架。
